Why the China storefront is not “just another locale”

App Store Connect treats each language as an independent row. Your en-US title, subtitle, keywords, and description do not auto-sync to zh-Hans. China Search vocabulary differs from US Search — literal en-US keyword translation rarely maps. Chinese buyers skim product pages differently: outcome-first openings beat feature bullet dumps copied from your settings screen. Screenshot galleries, App Preview captions, and IAP display names each have their own localization surfaces — but the core listing (name through What's New) is where most indie teams stall. You can ship binary updates without touching zh-Hans; you cannot expect China conversions with an empty or English-fallback row.

DIY ChatGPT vs Connect-ready human rewrite

The indie default workflow: export en-US from Connect, paste into ChatGPT with “translate to Simplified Chinese for App Store,” paste the reply into zh-Hans rows, save. Zero invoice, zero waiting. The hidden costs show up later.

  • Character limits: Models output prose without live counters. Title and subtitle cap around 30 characters each for zh-Hans; keywords around 100; promotional text at 170. You discover overflow when Connect flags the save — or when Search truncates mid-word.
  • Keyword strategy: LLMs repeat search nouns across every visible field. Apple’s hidden keyword row should carry synonyms your title and subtitle do not duplicate — models rarely split terms correctly for China Search.
  • 翻译腔 tone: Grammatically correct Simplified Chinese that still reads like a translated brochure — stacked adjectives, false cognates, English sentence order. Chinese users recognize template copy in one skim.
  • Trademark risk: “Better than Notion” or “Todoist alternative” becomes Chinese strings naming marks you do not own. Human rewrite flags a cut list before you submit.
  • Founder time: Fixing model output field by field often exceeds one day of solo dev time — more than the $79 one-time rewrite.

ChatGPT is fine for internal notes and stakeholder previews. It is a poor finish line for a storefront you enabled on purpose. See the full comparison on ChatGPT vs human zh-Hans rewrite.

AppLocale FAQ

Do I need a Chinese App Store listing to ship my iOS app to China?

You need a zh-Hans localization row in App Store Connect if you want Chinese users on the China storefront to see native copy. Enabling China under Pricing and Availability is separate from language — both matter. An empty zh-Hans row falls back to English, which converts poorly for Chinese buyers.

Can indie developers localize App Store Connect with ChatGPT?

ChatGPT works for internal drafts. Finished zh-Hans store copy needs Apple character limits enforced, idiomatic Simplified Chinese, and trademark-aware keyword packing. Models ignore Connect caps and produce 翻译腔 brochure tone. AppLocale is a one-time human rewrite delivered within 24 hours — paste-ready, not a model dump.
